editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq entered November 18 after a weak November 17 cash close, with negative market breadth and elevated volatility. Nvidia's stronger-than-expected earnings and forward guidance create a meaningful countertrend rally opportunity, but an extended-hours bounce is not yet a confirmed change in broad index trend.
editorial.whatChanged: A Bloomberg-syndicated report published at 07:20 IST described Nasdaq-100 futures up 1.3%, S&P futures up 0.7%, and Nvidia up more than 4% after hours. A separate Reuters Asia wrap described Nvidia down 0.5% after hours and Asian equities slightly lower. Their precise ticks and baselines differ or are unavailable, so these reports cannot be combined into a reliable time series or proof of a new reversal. Secondary daily November 17 Treasury yields were 5.10% for 10Y and 4.80% for 2Y, a +30bp spread, without claiming live verification.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The market is testing whether robust AI infrastructure demand can offset export restrictions, valuation pressure and broader risk aversion. Strong company earnings support a relief branch, but sustained SOX relative strength, broader participation and falling implied volatility are necessary for a credible bullish regime shift. A hawkish FOMC interpretation could offset the earnings benefit.
editorial.threeDayPath: Wednesday November 18 is the confirmation session: early semiconductor participation and the 14:00 EST FOMC minutes can generate a volatile two-way session. Thursday November 19 brings labor and Philadelphia Fed data that could reinforce or reverse the yield response. Friday November 20 should reveal whether the earnings rally broadens into a durable recovery or fades under renewed macro and sector selling.
editorial.bullCase: Nvidia guidance catalyzes durable SOX and QQQ outperformance, Nasdaq breadth turns positive and volatility compresses. Falling yields or a less-hawkish reading of FOMC minutes would help extend the rebound through Friday. This remains a conditional scenario rather than the verified baseline.
editorial.bearCase: An early futures-led bounce fails in cash trading, chip leadership remains narrow, and FOMC minutes or labor data support further tightening expectations. Weak breadth and high VIX would favor another leg lower, especially if the export-control and AI-financing concerns reassert themselves.
editorial.watchNext: Track November 18 synchronized QQQ/SOX and breadth after the cash open; compare VXN and VIX at the same timestamps; check official 2Y/10Y yields and direct CME FedWatch; watch 14:00 EST FOMC minutes and November 19 claims/Philadelphia Fed. Refresh paired Brent and WTI before drawing inflation conclusions. Review Open Watch for newly published material catalysts.
